builder_plan.scenario: A self-hosted assistant is too expensive because its model uses most of the GPU memory.
builder_plan.change: Try the paper's supported lower-precision weights on a copy of your serving setup.
builder_plan.baseline: The same model at its original precision, on the same GPU.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Peak memory, task pass rate, latency, and total serving cost at the same context and load.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: BReD: Block Replay Dithering for Stable Low-Bit EMA Optimizer States
summary: BReD replaces standard rounding in iterative low-bit optimizer-state quantization with block-wise subtractive dithering using deterministic seed replay, correcting the biased and amplified quantization-error accumulation in EMA-based states such as Adam moments. It costs little extra memory (no auxiliary random-tensor storage) and only modest implementation complexity via the authors' released code, with quality matching full-precision states at 4-bit in the reported experiments. Adoption can fail if the dithering integration interacts poorly with existing fused or sharded optimizer implementations, and 3-bit operation, while stable in the paper's settings, carries unproven risk on workloads outside the evaluated configurations.
rationale: If the reader fine-tunes 7B-class models with AdamW or Muon on a 24 GB GPU, 4-bit optimizer states with the released BReD implementation can materially relax the memory bottleneck, but the benefit is limited to training workloads and should be validated on their specific fine-tuning setup.

claims.statement: BReD replaces standard rounding in iterative low-bit optimizer-state quantization with block-wise subtractive dithering using deterministic seed replay, correcting the biased and amplified quantization-error accumulation in EMA-based states such as Adam moments. It costs little extra memory (no auxiliary random-tensor storage) and only modest implementation complexity via the authors' released code, with quality matching full-precision states at 4-bit in the reported experiments. Adoption can fail if the dithering integration interacts poorly with existing fused or sharded optimizer implementations, and 3-bit operation, while stable in the paper's settings, carries unproven risk on workloads outside the evaluated configurations.

4-bit BReD reduces optimizer-state storage roughly 8x versus FP32 while matching full-precision training (PPL shifts <=0.5 in pretraining, <=0.2 in fine-tuning, downstream changes within 0.7 points); 3-bit remains stable in evaluated settings.
